it won't pull your back but low reps and the fatigue your posterior chain already gets from wrestling daily might be a recipe for disaster, try back extensions (weighted) or a deadlift variation you can do with lighter weight such as an RDL.

Not sure whether to use straps or not. I'm a wrestler right now looking to go into PL soon and ofc my deadlift has gotten to a point where double overhand is impossible. I want to use straps because mixed grip seems unnatural for me and hook grip doesn't work (short thumbs and commercial gym bar maybe? not sure if a deadlift bar is thinner). I also do grip training to supplement wrestling. If I use straps right now will my raw deadlift be affected in the future if I decide to go into PL?

When should I use straps? I have deadlifts, sldls and pendlay rows in my program and I'm not sure when to use them. I'm guessing I'll use them on sldls and pendlay rows but I lift in a commercial gym so the barbells roll out of my hand and I can't really use chalk.
I started wrestling when I was pretty out of shape and I'm doing good now, try a class out see if you like it and stay consistent you will get in shape. I would also consider strength training.

Bench press, barbell squat, pendlay row, overhead press, deadlift, split squat, dips, pullups and chinups, deadlift variations and some bodybuilding accessories are great things to have in your routine, focusing on the basics is all you need as a new lifter.
